native.prompt_en: Design a diagram that depicts the concept of wave-particle duality. Tips: Quantum mechanics, light.

native.answer: Wave-particle duality is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics that describes how quantum entities like light and electrons exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. Light, traditionally viewed as a wave, exhibits diffraction and interference patterns, yet experiments like the photoelectric effect demonstrate it can also behave as a particle, known as photons. Similarly, electrons and other subatomic particles show wave-like behavior through phenomena like electron diffraction. The duality concept resolves through quantum theory which states that the properties observed depend on the experimental setup, rather than the inherent nature of the entity itself.

A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance. Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. Finally, YOLO learns very general representations of objects. It outperforms all other detection methods, including DPM and R-CNN, by a wide margin when generalizing from natural images to artwork on both the Picasso Dataset and the People-Art Dataset.

The task of object detection, which involves both localizing and classifying objects in an image, has seen great progress in recent years.
